name: MathlibAnnex.FDeriv.norm_apply_le_seminorm_of_lipschitz
title: A seminorm increment bound passes to every derivative direction

content.display_title: A seminorm increment bound passes to every derivative direction
content.one_sentence_role: Takes a difference-quotient limit without imposing a positive lower bound.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n,N\in\mathbb N_0$, let $E=\mathbb R^n$ and $F=\mathbb R^N$ have the sup norms, and let $p:E\to\mathbb R$ be a real seminorm. Let $f:E\to F$ satisfy
$$\|f(y)-f(z)\|_\infty\le p(y-z)\qquad(y,z\in E).$$
Fix a point $x\in E$ at which $f$ is Fréchet differentiable, and write $Df(x)$ for its derivative. Then
$$\|Df(x)v\|_\infty\le p(v)\qquad(v\in E).$$
content.assumptions: The seminorm may be degenerate. Neither norm equivalence nor a positive lower comparison is assumed. The increment estimate holds globally; differentiability is assumed only at the chosen point. Both dimensions may be zero.
content.conclusion: The same seminorm bounds $Df(x)v$ for every direction, including zero.
content.proof_summary: Apply the increment estimate on one affine line, then pass to its derivative.

proof_steps.text:
**Estimate one directional quotient.** Fix $v\in E$ and let $\phi(t)=f(x+tv)$. The increment assumption and seminorm homogeneity give
$$\|\phi(t)-\phi(0)\|_\infty\le p(tv)=|t|p(v).$$
For every real $t\ne0$, division by $|t|>0$ gives
$$\left\|\frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}\right\|_\infty\le p(v).$$
This also applies to $v=0$.

**Take the derivative limit.** Differentiability at $x$ gives
$$\frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}\longrightarrow Df(x)v\qquad(t\to0,\ t\ne0).$$
Continuity of the norm therefore yields
$$\|Df(x)v\|_\infty=\lim_{t\to0,\ t\ne0}\left\|\frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}\right\|_\infty\le p(v).$$
The source's local derivative-bound argument uses $\phi$, $d=Df(x)v$ and $C=p(v)$. The previous estimate and this derivative limit are its inputs; its output is exactly the asserted inequality.

content.lean_realization_notes: Let $\lambda_n$ denote coordinate Lebesgue measure on $E$. [The separate almost-everywhere wrapper](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/SeminormBound.lean#L60-L71) additionally takes $U\ge0$ with $p(z)\le U\|z\|_\infty$. Then $\|f(y)-f(z)\|_\infty\le U\|y-z\|_\infty$, so Rademacher gives differentiability almost everywhere for reference Lebesgue measure. Restriction to any set $s\subseteq E$ and the pointwise result give the bound for every $v$, for $\lambda_n|_s$-almost every $x$. The extra upper comparison is an input of this wrapper.
